newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic job assurances cited by union.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic job assurances cited by union.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp have agreed in writing that their planned merger would not result in involuntary layoffs of union members at least through August 1998, the Communications Workers of America on Tuesday.
The union said in a statement it intended to negotiate a new agreement next summer to extend that commitment, which was made earlier in the merger process.

The union issued its statement after the two companies denied a Wall Street Journal report that they eventually would cut 10,000 or more union and non-union jobs as a result of the merger, rather than the 3,000 non-union jobs they originally announced. Their current combined workforce is 137,000. The Journal report was attributed to "people familiar with the companies' employment plans."

The union said it had assurances from the companies that the merger was "not a predatory slash-and-burn strategy for the short-term gratification of Wall Street speculators." The union said it intended to hold the companies to those assurances.
